verdicts.statement: For every integer N >= 2, the maximal quotient ring \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN} is the largest quotient of the Laurent polynomial ring \Liq for which the image of the level-N quantum trace is a knot invariant. Concretely, the image \widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(L)(q,s) of the level-N quantum trace in \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN} is a knot invariant, and any other quotient \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}' of \Li in which \widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(\beta_n) is a knot invariant factors through \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN} (universal/maximality property).

verdicts.statement: The level-N unified invariant \Omega_{\cN}(L)(q,s) \in \Li_{\cN} is a well-defined oriented knot invariant that globalises the N-th coloured Jones and coloured Alexander (ADO) invariants, via the identity \Omega_{\cN}(L)(q,s) = J_{N}(L,q) + \Phi_{N}(L,s) - \Phi_{N}(L, q^{1-N}).

verdicts.statement: For the level-N sequence of braid group representations { \widetilde\rho_{\cN,n} | n \in \N }, there exists a quantum trace \qptr_{V_{\cN}^{\otimes n}} that is unique up to a scalar multiple. Equivalently, for any quantum trace associated to \widetilde{V}_{\cN}^{\otimes n} there is a non-zero element g_0(q,s) \in \Li_{\cN} such that \qptr(f) = \sum_{j=0}^{\cN-1} g_0(q,s) q^{-2i} f on the relevant matrix coefficients.
